name: Piramal Finance Ltd
title: Piramal Finance Ltd - 544597 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Piramal Finance Q4 FY26: Growth RoAUM rose to 2.1% (from 1.7% a year ago) with AUM up 25% and FY27 guidance of ~25% AUM growth and ~2.5% exit RoAUM; capital consumption only 50 bps in the quarter.

triggers.label: Retail disbursements up 34% YoY
triggers.quote: Disbursements in retail recovered from a moderate Q3 and were up 34% year-on-year to INR13,101 crores

triggers.label: AA+ could cut borrowing cost 50-80 bps

summary.headline: Piramal Finance FY26 consol net profit rose to INR1,506 crore (3x YoY); Q4 Growth RoAUM 2.1%, with FY27 exit guidance of 2.5%.
summary.overview: Consolidated AUM grew 25% YoY to about INR1,01,230 crore, with Growth AUM up 33% to INR98,423 crore and the Legacy book cut 59% to INR2,807 crore. Q4 Growth PBT was INR495 crore (up 61% YoY) and consolidated net profit was INR502 crore versus INR102 crore a year earlier. Management attributed the step-up in profit partly to one-time gains from the Piramal Imaging deferred consideration and the Shriram Life stake sale, part of which was used to take markdowns and build buffers. Domestic ratings moved to AA+ across all three agencies, and FY27 guidance is ~25% AUM growth, ~50% consol profit growth and ~2.5% exit RoAUM.

segments.name: Retail (Growth)
segments.commentary: Retail AUM INR85,885 crore (85% of total), up 33% YoY; Q4 disbursements INR13,101 crore (+34% YoY). Retail 90+ DPD 0.6%, down 20 bps QoQ; retail opex/AUM 3.6%, down 21 bps QoQ.

segments.name: Mortgages (HL + LAP)
segments.commentary: Mortgage AUM INR57,837 crore, up 32% YoY; 57% of total AUM and 67% of retail AUM. Smaller-ticket MSME mortgages, previously flagged, stabilised in Q4.

segments.name: Wholesale 2.0
segments.commentary: AUM INR12,538 crore, up 38% YoY; real estate:CMML mix 73:27, average ticket INR53 crore, yield 14.4%, zero NPAs. FY26 disbursements INR9,292 crore; repayments INR5,859 crore (about 63% of disbursements).

segments.name: Legacy
segments.commentary: AUM INR2,807 crore, down 59% YoY and under 3% of total AUM (66% four years ago). Management expects it to become immaterial by Q4 FY27 and to stop separate reporting during FY27.

segments.name: Gold and rural (new)
segments.commentary: Gold loans: 22 branches launched in Maharashtra and Telangana (13 disbursement-active), target about 200 branches in FY27. Rural: 136 branches; micro loans AUM INR1,384 crore, up 42% YoY.

guidance_outlook: FY27: total AUM growth of about 25% YoY.
FY27: consolidated profit growth of about 50%.
Exit FY27 at about 2.5% RoAUM (vs 2.1% in Q4 FY26); management says this holds even with some credit cost normalisation.
Rating upgrade to AA+ could cut cost of borrowing by 50-80 bps as the liability stack churns over about three years; steady-state ROE could rise 3-4 percentage points.
Retail opex/AUM expected to fall a little further in FY27; management cites about 50 bps more room. Unsecured mix to rise 400-500 bps.
Tax: about INR16,000 crore of future profit is shielded by accumulated losses (about INR24,500 crore gross); effective tax rate can be modelled very low until about 2032.
capex_capacity: Branch network 701 at March 2026 (crossed 700 in Q4); Q4 added 26 urban full-service, 22 gold and 60 rural branches; management target about 880 branches per the presentation.
Gold loans: plan to add about 180 branches in FY27 to reach about 200; a gold branch costs about one-third of an urban branch's annual opex.
Rural branches cost about one-tenth of an urban branch to set up.
Capital: CRAR 19.8%; management would consider raising capital at 17.5-18%. Net capital consumption in Q4 was only 50 bps, giving roughly 3-4 quarters of runway.
Net worth to net owned funds gap (INR2,500-2,700 crore each from BAU deductions, DTA of INR2,700 crore, and investments) should narrow by about one-third as investments are divested.
demand_pricing: Wholesale repayments are strong: Q4 repayments were about 82% of Q4 disbursements, and about 50% of FY27 contractual repayments are already received.
Digital unsecured loans are performing well, but management will cut them quickly if risk curves turn (it cut digital by over 60% in FY25).
Cross-sell is about 30% of unsecured disbursements, expected to rise materially.
Watch list expanded beyond F&B MSMEs to travel and logistics, textiles, gems and jewellery, and food processing. Bounce rates in April matched March; no visible retail risk impact yet.
Management expects any Middle East war effect on unsecured 90+ DPD to show around July-August (Q2), not in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What drives Growth NIM beyond 7%, and does consol NIM converge with it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects consol and Growth NIM to converge in the latter half of FY27. Levers are asset mix (unsecured +400-500 bps, gold) and cost of borrowing, with AA+ benefit of 50-80 bps over about three years.

qa_highlights.question: Q4 fee income looked low as a share of retail AUM; where should it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 was depressed by a one-time reversal of fee income to help its 50%-owned life insurance associate. Fee income should return to normal, and the 70-90 bps level was seen as reasonable.

qa_highlights.question: Can the 2.5% exit RoAUM hold if credit cost rises toward 1.9-2%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said opex/AUM (about 50 bps more to go) and cost of borrowing gains should absorb the credit cost normalisation. Mix is shifting toward prime-like mortgages.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for capital and the net worth to NOF gap?
qa_highlights.answer: CRAR is 19.8%; the gap between net worth and NOF comes from BAU deductions, DTA of about INR2,700 crore and investments. The company has 3-4 quarters of runway before the 17.5-18% raise trigger.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the INR900 crore fair-value loss and INR590 crore impairment in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described them as pre-emptive markdowns made with the one-time gains (about INR1,300 crore deferred Imaging consideration and about INR250-300 crore Shriram Life gain). About one-third is added buffer; the rest is losses that would have come over two years.

qa_highlights.question: Will branch expansion push up opex/AUM?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Opex/AUM is expected to keep falling in FY27. If the two conflict, management will prioritise the opex curve over branch openings.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict: crude and LPG supply, and second-order effects on self-employed and business borrowers, mainly in Q2 FY27.
Q4 credit cost of 1.5% is below the 1.9-2% steady state management cited; any normalisation cuts into the RoAUM path.
Bond market access at AA+ is still untested; no bond issue since the upgrade, and the cost-of-borrowing benefit depends on churn.
Q4 profit included one-time gains and markdowns; sustainability of the consolidated profit growth (about 50%) depends on the Growth book.
Capital: CRAR 19.8% vs 15% requirement; capital raise possible if CRAR falls to 17.5-18%.
Legacy book write-backs of a few hundred crore are expected, but there is no timing.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on delivery against FY26 targets and the FY27 framework, but cautious on the Middle East conflict, which they describe as a Q2 risk to watch. Management was direct on capital and opex, and more guarded on timing for the write-backs and M&A.
key_quotes: Asset quality of Wholesale 2.0 continues to remain robust with zero NPAs in this book.

We expect another year of approximately 25% growth in total AUM. We expect consol profits to also grow at approximately 50%, and we expect to exit FY27 with a return on AUM of approximately 2.5% versus the 2.1% we reported in Q4 FY26.

Domestic credit rating upgrade from AA to AA+ has the potential to lower our cost of borrowing by 50 to 80 basis points once we churn our current borrowing stack out and replace it with new borrowings.
So, watching a 90 day delinquency metric, it is not going to move anytime soon. My guess is July -August is when you can actually see that outcome, if at all.
